paragraphs.title: A Call to Righteousness and Openness to Those Who Seek God

answers: To keep judgment and do justice
To build a wall around the city
easy.explanation: The Lord says, “Keep ye judgment, and do justice.”
easy.q: What does the Lord command in verse 1?

easy.explanation: The verse says that he “keepeth the sabbath from polluting it.”
easy.q: What is the blessed man commanded to keep from polluting?

easy.explanation: The blessed man “keepeth his hand from doing any evil.”
easy.q: From what should a person keep his hand?

answers: Because the Lord’s salvation is near to come
Because the Sabbath is no longer needed
medium.explanation: The Lord connects this command with the statement, “my salvation is near to come.”
medium.q: Why should people keep judgment and do justice?

answers: He works only during the day
medium.explanation: The phrase means that the person refrains from doing evil.
medium.q: What does the phrase “keepeth his hand from doing any evil” mean?

answers: The man who does these things and holds fast to them
The man who avoids the house of prayer
medium.explanation: The verse begins, “Blessed is the man that doeth this,” and describes one who holds fast to it.
medium.q: Who is called blessed in verse 2?

answers: Serving God includes justice, righteousness, Sabbath observance, and avoiding evil
Serving God is concerned only with where a person lives
Serving God requires giving up justice
challenge.explanation: The verses join justice, righteousness, Sabbath observance, and avoiding evil as marks of faithful living.
challenge.q: What connection do these verses make between righteous actions and serving God?

challenge.explanation: The general wording presents the call as applying broadly to human beings.
challenge.q: To whom does the wording “the man” and “the son of man” apply?

challenge.explanation: The Lord says, “my salvation is near to come.”
challenge.q: What does the Lord say is near to come?

paragraphs.title: Welcoming Eunuchs and Foreigners into God’s House

answers: Eunuchs and foreigners who hold fast to His covenant
easy.explanation: The passage promises blessing to eunuchs and the sons of the stranger who keep the Lord’s covenant.
easy.q: To whom does the Lord promise a place and a name in His house?

easy.explanation: The Lord says, “I will give in mine house and within my walls a place and a name.”
easy.q: What will the Lord give the eunuchs in His house and within His walls?

answers: An house of prayer for all people
A house of war for all people
A house of trade for all people
easy.explanation: Verse 7 says, “mine house shall be called an house of prayer for all people.”
easy.q: What will God’s house be called?

answers: They keep the Sabbath and hold fast to the covenant
They leave the house of prayer
medium.explanation: Both groups are described as keeping the Sabbath and taking hold of the Lord’s covenant.
medium.q: What common condition is mentioned concerning the eunuchs and foreigners?

answers: A name and remembrance that will not be cut off
The name of a particular place
A name that lasts for only one day
medium.explanation: The Lord promises a name “that shall not be cut off,” indicating lasting remembrance.
medium.q: What does “an everlasting name” mean in this passage?

answers: They will serve Him and love His name
medium.explanation: They join themselves to the Lord “to serve him, and to love the name of the Lord.”
medium.q: What will the sons of the stranger do when they join themselves to the Lord?

answers: Those from every people who seek God may approach Him
There is no place for prayer there
challenge.explanation: The phrase “for all people” expresses an openness to people from every nation who come to worship God.
challenge.q: What idea is expressed by calling God’s house “an house of prayer for all people”?

answers: God welcomes foreigners while continuing to gather the outcasts of Israel
Welcoming foreigners cancels the gathering of Israel
The gathering of Israel prevents all prayer
challenge.explanation: After describing foreigners joining themselves to the Lord, the passage says that He will also gather Israel’s outcasts.
challenge.q: How are the welcoming of foreigners and the gathering of Israel related?

answers: Keeping the Sabbath, choosing what pleases God, and holding fast to His covenant
challenge.explanation: The promise is connected with their faithfulness: they keep the Sabbath, choose what pleases God, and hold fast to His covenant.
challenge.q: What enables the eunuchs to receive a place and lasting remembrance in God’s house?

paragraphs.title: Criticism of Greedy and Sleeping Leaders

easy.explanation: The watchmen are called blind, ignorant, dumb dogs, and lovers of sleep.
easy.q: How are the leaders described in these verses?

easy.explanation: The passage says, “they are all dumb dogs, they cannot bark.”
easy.q: What can the dumb dogs not do?

answers: Praying in the house of God
easy.explanation: They say, “I will fetch wine, and we will fill ourselves with strong drink.”
easy.q: What are the leaders doing at the end of the passage?

answers: Because they neither understand nor warn others
Because they guard the people well
Because they lead the people in prayer
medium.explanation: They are blind, ignorant, and unable to bark, showing that they fail to understand or give warning.
medium.q: Why is describing the leaders as blind and dumb dogs a criticism?

answers: Each person pursues his own profit
medium.explanation: The phrase means that each leader seeks personal gain rather than caring for others.
medium.q: What does “every one for his gain” mean?

medium.explanation: The verse says, “they all look to their own way, every one for his gain.”
medium.q: What does each leader look to according to verse 11?

answers: A failure to warn people about danger
Joy in the house of prayer
challenge.explanation: A watch dog that cannot bark cannot give warning, symbolizing the leaders’ failure to protect the people.
challenge.q: What does the inability of the dogs to bark symbolize?

answers: Ignorance, pursuit of personal gain, drinking, and drunkenness
Gathering the outcasts, serving God, and rejoicing
challenge.explanation: The passage presents leaders who do not understand, pursue their own gain, and then indulge in drink.
challenge.q: Which sequence best describes the leaders’ decline?

answers: They expect their prosperity to continue despite their corruption
challenge.explanation: Their confident prediction about tomorrow emphasizes their self-indulgence and misplaced confidence.
challenge.q: What does their expectation that tomorrow will be “much more abundant” reveal?
